newsitem.title: OMAN: Shell Oman in IPO, trading to start in October.
newsitem.headline: Shell Oman in IPO, trading to start in October.

text.p: Shell Oman Marketing Co has opened for subscription and its shares are expected to start trading on the Muscat Securities Market in October, the firm said on Sunday.
In a statement, it said 40 percent of its shares opened for public subscription on Saturday. Royal Dutch/Shell Group will retain 49 percent in the new firm.
Shell Oman Marketing is being formed to buy the businesses of Shell Marketing (Oman) Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Anglo-Dutch oil group, and of the Oman Lubricants Company LLC.
Oman Lubricants is owned 55 percent by Shell and 45 percent by Omani businessmen.
The balance in the new firm will be held by shareholders in the lubricants firm, filling station dealers and employees.
The company is being set up with a capital of 10 million shares at 4.9 rials per share and the public share offer is worth 19.6 million rials, the statement said.

"The prospectus projects a dividend of 529 baisas per share for the year to December 31, 1998, the first full year of operations," it said, adding a dividend of 130 baisas for the last three months of 1997 was also projected.
The share issue is open to Omani citizens, Omani companies and branches of foreign companies registered in the Gulf Arab state.
Public subscription opened on July 19 and will close on August 17, the statement said.
